documents.title: Set up an external agent
documents.summary: Let Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity or another CLI harness drive Capturefab. Keep the desktop open to review captures and intervene.
documents.body: Set up an external agent Let Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity or another CLI harness drive Capturefab. Keep the desktop open to review captures and intervene. Your harness supplies model access. Capturefab provider credentials are unnecessary for this route. The built-in AI assistant has separate provider settings. Your harness controls whether its model receives images and tool results. 1. Make the CLI available Install Capturefab for a visible workspace. On a computer without a display, the same download lists the CLI commands. Add the executable directory to your harness's PATH , or give it the executable's full path. capturefab --version capturefab doctor --json capturefab tools list --compact --json capturefab tools describe capture_photos --json tools list --compact lists names, risk classes and session requirements. tools describe NAME returns one argument schema. For an older build without these options, use tools list --json . Read the installed --help for supported commands. 2. Open a shared workspace If the app is open, choose Help → Connect an Agent… . Select Copy agent briefing for its executable path and session name. Give that briefing to your harness. For a new visible workspace, run this command in its own terminal. Keep that terminal open: capturefab gui --name bench For a headless session, use capturefab serve --name bench . If the app is already open, run capturefab sessions --json . Use its session name instead of starting another camera connection. 3. Give the agent a bounded first task Give your harness the agent instructions and this task. Replace bench if your session has another name. Use Capturefab session bench as actor capture-agent with actor kind agent. Work only with simulator camera sim:0. Read the installed tool catalog. Connect the camera and examine a fresh image with inspect_frame. Save two PNG images named first-{seq}.png in your working directory. Use the working directory only. Keep the existing storage limits. Report the saved paths and errors. Leave the session open for manual review. Use --session bench --actor capture-agent --actor-kind agent on external-agent calls. Tool arguments select the camera; omit global --camera and unset CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA . Read the full camera tools procedure for exact calls. 4. Review and take over Open Activity to review the named agent's actions, saved paths and failures. Examine the returned inspection image before accepting image-quality claims. CLI tool captures use the calling harness's working directory. The built-in assistant uses the app's configured capture folder. To intervene, stop the external harness's task first. An accepted camera command can still finish. Examine status and jobs before changing settings or retrying a capture. capturefab --session bench status --json capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 jobs --json capturefab --session bench activity --json Cancel only the job or recording you intend to stop. Do not quit the shared session while another participant's work is active. For analysis data, continue with plant data for analysis .

documents.title: Your first capture
documents.summary: Connect a camera. Examine its image. Save a frame. The built-in pattern camera supplies images without camera hardware.
documents.body: Start here Your first capture Connect a camera. Examine its image. Save a frame. The built-in pattern camera supplies images without camera hardware. Install and open the desktop app for your operating system and processor. Enter sim:0 in the camera address field. Push Enter to connect the pattern camera. Select the camera. Open Features to examine its settings. Open Capture . Keep File names at By date, camera and time (recommended) , with Frames at 1 and Format at PNG. Select Capture & save . Capture acquires a frame when the preview is stopped. The path below the save button shows the saved file. Each capture gets a new name, and Capturefab does not overwrite existing files. # Find cameras, including the built-in simulator capturefab discover --simulate # The same first capture from a terminal; run it again for first-0002.png capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'first-{seq}.png' # Examine the simulator, then capture a sequence capturefab --camera sim:0 features capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -n 10 -o first-frames These commands automatically use the only active desktop or headless session. Its preview and Activity show the work. Without an active session, capture uses a temporary camera worker. Use --direct for a temporary worker. With several sessions, use --session NAME . Local output paths use the directory of the terminal that sends the command. Screenshots show the current development app with simulator sources. Controls can differ by release.

documents.title: Camera data for analysis
documents.summary: Capture images and video with camera identity, timestamps and tags. Export the catalog, with the images, as a folder you can train from.
documents.body: Start here Camera data for analysis Capture images and video with camera identity, timestamps and tags. Export the catalog, with the images, as a folder you can train from. Connect a camera and choose a capture folder. Fill in Capture tags and select Capture or Record. With File names › One folder per label , each Label gets its own folder. Open Dataset to review the saved-file catalog, or select Export… to copy it and the images to a new folder. capturefab serve --name line1 --dataset plant.duckdb capturefab --session line1 --camera sim:0 capture -o 'line1/{tag:part}/{camera}-{seq}.png' --context part=A-100 capturefab --session line1 dataset query "SELECT camera_id, path, wall_ms FROM captures LIMIT 20" capturefab --session line1 dataset export -o exports/shift-b --media images --group-by part

documents.title: Upgrade to version 0.4.0
documents.summary: Version 0.4.0 removes built-in file uploads and industrial signal sources. Camera capture, recording, datasets and folder destinations remain available.
documents.body: Upgrade to version 0.4.0 Version 0.4.0 removes built-in file uploads and industrial signal sources. Camera capture, recording, datasets and folder destinations remain available. S3, FTP and SFTP destinations and their transfer queue are no longer available. Legacy transfers do not resume in this version. The upgrade does not delete their queued local files. Review pending transfers before upgrading a working installation. Use an external transfer tool for files that still need to reach another system. Saved folder destinations remain available on local disks, removable drives and mounted network drives. Entries for removed destination types are ignored. Live industrial signal inputs are no longer available. Use separate signal-collection tools if your workflow depends on those inputs. Existing owned capture files remain subject to the storage budget. Retain backups of files and configuration when changing a production installation.

documents.title: Install and verify a release
documents.summary: Every download includes the app and the command-line interface (CLI). On a computer without a display, the same executable works as a CLI.
documents.body: Start here Install and verify a release Every download includes the app and the command-line interface (CLI). On a computer without a display, the same executable works as a CLI. For an existing installation, read the version 0.4.0 upgrade notes before replacing the executable. From a terminal, one command picks the build for this computer, checks its SHA-256 before extracting and installs it for your account. It never uses sudo or administrator rights. # macOS and Linux: the app in ~/Applications or ~/.local/share/capturefab, the command in ~/.local/bin curl -fsSL https://capturefab.com/install.sh | sh # Windows PowerShell: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Capturefab, on your user PATH irm https://capturefab.com/install.ps1 | iex To read the script first, download it, then run it: curl -fsSLO https://capturefab.com/install.sh; less install.sh; sh install.sh . --dry-run prints the file, URL and checksum it would use; --prefix DIR and --bin-dir DIR choose other folders. To download by hand, the download page lists release files and their SHA-256 checksums. Select the build for your installed operating system and processor architecture. Apple silicon uses ARM64. Intel and AMD PCs usually use x64. On Raspberry Pi and Jetson, a 64-bit processor can have a 32-bit operating system. To learn about later versions, see update checks . To check a download by hand, run the command for your system in the download's folder: # Linux echo "EXPECTED_SHA256 DOWNLOADED_FILE" | sha256sum -c # macOS echo "EXPECTED_SHA256 DOWNLOADED_FILE" | shasum -a 256 -c # Windows PowerShell if ((Get-FileHash .\DOWNLOADED_FILE -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq 'EXPECTED_SHA256') { 'OK: checksum matches' } else { 'MISMATCH: do not open this file' } The download selector and the download page fill in the file name and checksum for you. Linux and macOS print OK for a match; anything else means do not open the file. With the release's SHA256SUMS file in the same folder, sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS or shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS checks every download there. Then open the disk image (macOS) or extract the archive (Windows, Linux and earlier macOS releases). Keep the included license files with the application; on macOS they are inside Capturefab.app/Contents/Resources/licenses . Install the download System Steps macOS Open the .dmg file and drag Capturefab.app to Applications. Open it from Applications, then eject the disk image. Releases up to 0.4.0 are a .zip instead: extract it, move Capturefab.app to Applications and open it. The capturefab file beside it in the .zip is a CLI launcher for the app in the same folder; after the move, use the command inside the app. Windows Extract the .zip file. Open capturefab.exe from the extracted folder. In PowerShell, run .\capturefab.exe from that folder. A build marked Unsigned on the download page can trigger a SmartScreen prompt; verify the checksum, then choose More info → Run anyway . Linux Extract the .tar.gz file. Open a terminal in the extracted folder. Run ./capturefab . If necessary, set executable permission with chmod +x ./capturefab . First launch: system prompts The first time Capturefab opens or reaches a camera, your system can ask for permission. These answers decide whether cameras appear. Prompts on first launch System What to expect Windows A build marked Unsigned on the download page can show Windows protected your PC from SmartScreen. Check the SHA-256 first, then choose More info → Run anyway . Or, after checking, run Unblock-File .\capturefab.exe in PowerShell. The PowerShell installer needs neither. When Windows Defender Firewall asks, allow Capturefab on Private networks . GigE Vision and RTSP-over-UDP video arrive as inbound UDP; blocking it shows up as connection or stream timeouts. USB3 Vision cameras must use the WinUSB driver on their camera interfaces. In Device Manager, or with a WinUSB installer such as Zadig, select the camera's interfaces and install WinUSB. This replaces the vendor's driver, so the vendor's own software stops seeing the camera until you undo it: Device Manager › the camera › Update driver or Roll back driver . macOS Allow Local Network when asked. GigE Vision, ONVIF, RTSP, hub and scanner discovery need it; without it, discovery finds nothing on the network. Allow Camera when asked to use webcams. To change either later, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network or Camera , turn Capturefab on and reopen the app. Linux There are no prompts, but USB3 Vision cameras need device permissions and GigE Vision needs a larger socket receive buffer. Run capturefab doctor : it checks both and prints the command for each fix. The line computer guide explains the udev rule and net.core.rmem_max . Use the CLI from any terminal The installers above already put capturefab on your PATH . After a manual download, link or copy it into a folder on your PATH to use the shorter commands in these guides. # macOS, after moving Capturefab.app to Applications mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && ln -sf /Applications/Capturefab.app/Contents/MacOS/capturefab ~/.local/bin/capturefab # Linux, from the extracted folder install -Dm755 ./capturefab ~/.local/bin/capturefab # Windows PowerShell, from the extracted folder $dir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Capturefab" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null; Copy-Item -Recurse -Force .\* $dir $path = (Get-Item HKCU:\Environment).GetValue('Path', '', 'DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames') New-ItemProperty HKCU:\Environment Path -PropertyType ExpandString -Value "$path;$dir" -Force | Out-Null Then open a new terminal and run capturefab --version . If it is not found on macOS or Linux, add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" to ~/.zshrc or ~/.profile . On Linux, copy the extracted share/ folder into ~/.local/share/ for a launcher entry, as INSTALL-DESKTOP.txt describes. For the current terminal only, run export PATH="$PWD:$PATH" in the extracted folder, or $env:Path = "$PWD;$env:Path" in PowerShell. Without a display, running the executable with no subcommand prints CLI help. This includes SSH sessions on Linux. Use an explicit subcommand such as doctor --json or serve . To run serve as a Linux service, follow the line computer guide . It covers Raspberry Pi, Jetson, industrial PCs and access from a laptop browser. For an agent harness on macOS, use the ~/.local/bin/capturefab link above or /Applications/Capturefab.app/Contents/MacOS/capturefab as the executable path. A copy run straight from the mounted disk image has a /Volumes path that stops working when you eject it. Run your harness under the same operating-system account as the local session. Minimum operating system versions Build Minimum requirement macOS ARM64 macOS 11.0 macOS x64 macOS 10.15 Windows x64 Windows 10; Windows 11 on ARM can use x64 emulation. Windows ARM64 Windows 11 on ARM Linux x64 and ARM64 glibc 2.28; examples include Debian 10, RHEL 8 and Jetson Linux R34. These minimums also apply to the included FFmpeg executable. A separate Visual C++ redistributable is not necessary for Windows builds. There is no 32-bit ARM build. On Debian-based Linux, run dpkg --print-architecture . Use the ARM64 build if the result is arm64 . If it is armhf , install a supported 64-bit operating system first. A 64-bit processor alone does not establish operating system compatibility. See the release target details for build requirements. Release builds include a separate FFmpeg executable. Separate Aravis, FFmpeg, libusb, vendor SDK and Python installations are not necessary. The operating system must have suitable graphics and camera drivers. Document scanners have additional driver requirements . capturefab --version capturefab doctor --json # Optional: verify GitHub build provenance gh attestation verify DOWNLOADED_FILE --repo capturefab/capturefab For a source build, see Build, architecture & licensing .

documents.title: Check for updates
documents.summary: The desktop app looks for a new version at most once a day. It shows what it finds and never downloads or installs anything itself.
documents.body: Start here Check for updates The desktop app looks for a new version at most once a day. It shows what it finds and never downloads or installs anything itself. What is sent. One GET of the public release list, https://capturefab.com/releases.json , with no account, device, usage or version information, no cookies and no query string. Like any website visit, the server sees your IP address. The first automatic check runs shortly after launch; a failed check waits a day like a successful one. What you see. When a new version exists, a short notice appears once and the menu item reads Update Available . Check for Updates… (application menu on macOS, Help menu on Windows and Linux) opens the highlights, a download link for this computer and the release notes. Skip This Version silences that version until a newer one appears. Verify and install. Downloads come from the GitHub release. Compare the SHA-256 shown in the app with SHA256SUMS as in Install and verify , then install it the same way you installed this version. Turn it off. Clear Check for new versions automatically in Settings › Updates . For managed installs, CAPTUREFAB_UPDATE_CHECK=off or a policy file containing {"update_check":"off"} turns off automatic and requested checks: /Library/Application Support/Capturefab/policy.json on macOS, /etc/capturefab/policy.json on Linux, %ProgramData%\Capturefab\policy.json on Windows. Apps opened from the Finder do not read shell variables, so use the policy file there. From a terminal. The CLI and serve never check on their own. capturefab version prints this version and the last result offline; capturefab version --check reads the list once. capturefab doctor warns when a newer version is known.

documents.title: Understand the workspace
documents.summary: Each window shows one camera, with its preview between a capture sidebar and a features inspector. Open another window for each additional camera.
documents.body: Start here Understand the workspace Each window shows one camera, with its preview between a capture sidebar and a features inspector. Open another window for each additional camera. A simulator camera streams in its own window. Its controls stay beside its preview. Camera picker A window without a camera lists discovered and recently used sources. Enter an IP address, stream URL or video file to connect directly. Preview stage Shows this window’s camera. Streaming state, frame rate and errors belong to each camera. Sidebar At left, Capture saves images and schedules, and Video records video or publishes a stream. Inspector At right, Features edits camera settings. Common controls appear first; expand the labeled sections for additional settings. Each panel has its own toggle in the title bar; in a narrower window they float over the preview. Activity See human and AI agent actions across the session’s cameras, including progress, saved files and full errors. Choose File › Connect to Camera… to open another camera picker. The shortcut is ⌘N / Ctrl+N . Selecting a camera that another window already shows brings that window forward. Capture saves from this window’s camera. Capture All saves one frame from every connected camera. Its shortcut is ⇧⌘S / Ctrl+Shift+S . Closing a camera window disconnects that camera. The app asks first if a recording is active. Closing the last window quits the app. See the window reference for close decisions and the menu reference for available actions. The app uses your system’s light or dark appearance. It saves workspace settings and recent camera addresses. It does not save addresses with credentials or secret query parameters. To set the appearance at startup, use CAPTUREFAB_APPEARANCE=light or dark .

documents.title: Find and connect cameras
documents.summary: Discovery lists GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, native and ONVIF cameras, document scanners and cameras on saved hubs. Connect a listed source or enter its address.
documents.body: Connect & examine Find and connect cameras Discovery lists GigE Vision, USB3 Vision, native and ONVIF cameras, document scanners and cameras on saved hubs. Connect a listed source or enter its address. The camera picker lists found sources above the direct-address field. Enable Include simulated cameras in Settings to discover Pattern cameras without hardware. Open a window on the camera picker; select Search again to repeat discovery. Read the discovery warnings. Select a listed camera to connect it in this window. Start its stream for a continuous preview. Push ⌘N / Ctrl+N to connect another camera in a new window. Stop acquisition before you change camera geometry or a native video mode. Camera compatibility describes connection requirements and unsupported paths. capturefab discover --json capturefab native --json # webcams and capture cards capturefab onvif discover --json # ONVIF devices on the LAN capturefab scanners --json capturefab hub cameras --json # cameras on saved hubs capturefab --simulate discover # include the pattern camera # Reuse an open desktop session capturefab sessions capturefab --session gui connect sim:0 capturefab --session gui start Select a camera by its discovered ID, unique serial number or GigE IPv4 address. A GigE camera must have a reachable address on its subnet. USB3 Vision uses userspace access. Linux must have USB permissions. macOS must have an available IOKit interface. Windows must have WinUSB on the camera's interfaces . Native webcams can also need operating system camera permission. On macOS and Windows, when the system refuses a webcam, the welcome screen shows Open Camera Settings . Allow access there, then select the camera again. Windows: assign WinUSB. When connect says Windows is not using WinUSB, another driver, usually the camera vendor's, holds the camera's USB3 Vision interface. Close vendor camera software first. Use the vendor's driver tool if it can switch the camera to WinUSB. Otherwise run Zadig : choose Options › List All Devices , select the camera's interface, choose WinUSB and select Replace Driver . Reconnect the camera and discover again. Vendor software that needs its own driver cannot open the camera until you roll the driver back in Device Manager. Camera commands automatically use the only active GUI or headless session. With several sessions, use --session NAME . Use --direct --camera ID for a temporary connection. Camera control can be exclusive. If the app has the camera open, use its session. --camera ID targets a camera and keeps the visible selection. select ID sets the session default for CLI calls without --camera . Desktop windows and browser tabs each keep their own selection. disconnect releases the addressed camera.

documents.title: Camera and media source locators
documents.summary: A source locator identifies the camera, stream or file to open. Put locators with spaces or URL query parameters in quotation marks.
documents.body: Connect & examine Camera and media source locators A source locator identifies the camera, stream or file to open. Put locators with spaces or URL query parameters in quotation marks. Source examples Source Locator What to check Simulator sim:0 , sim:1 Built in; useful for learning and scripts. GigE / USB3 Vision Discovered ID, serial or 192.168.1.10 Network reachability or USB access. macOS webcam 'avfoundation:FaceTime HD Camera' Use the ID returned by native or discover ; quote IDs that contain spaces. The index form avfoundation:0 also works. Linux webcam v4l2:/dev/video0 A supported host video driver and permission. Windows webcam dshow:video=Camera Name Use the exact device name. Network stream rtsp://camera/live , srt://host:8890 Reachable stream and protocol support in FFmpeg. ONVIF onvif:http://camera/onvif/device_service HTTP SOAP endpoint and resolvable media profile. Camera hub hub:home/camera.front_door A Home Assistant, Frigate, go2rtc or UniFi Protect server saved as a hub; see Camera hubs . Video file /path/to/clip.mp4 A readable file with a format FFmpeg can decode. Choose a native camera mode Native locators accept ?size=1280x720&fps=30 . Examine Features for available VideoMode choices. Before acquisition, select a supported mode. You can also set supported Width , Height and AcquisitionFrameRate values. Available modes depend on the driver. V4L2 format listings do not establish frame-rate limits. capturefab --camera 'avfoundation:0?size=1280x720&fps=30' capture -o webcam.png capturefab --camera 'rtsp://camera/live' capture -o network.png capturefab --camera '/path/to/clip.mp4' capture -o video-frame.png capturefab onvif resolve 'http://camera/onvif/device_service' --username admin --json When an RTSP or ONVIF camera asks for a user name and password, the desktop app opens Sign in to camera ; Remember on this computer saves the sign-in in the OS credential store once the camera connects. From the command line, capturefab login add rtsp://camera/live --user admin --password-stdin checks and saves a sign-in, and later --camera rtsp://camera/live uses it automatically; login list and login remove manage them. login add and onvif resolve also read the password from CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA_PASSWORD . A camera that asks for a sign-in fails with auth_required and one that refuses it with auth_rejected , both exit 1. Locators also accept one-time credentials, onvif://USER:PASS@HOST/onvif/device_service , with percent encoding for reserved characters; these are never saved. The interface and status hide credentials, but your shell can record typed secrets. A saved password is sent to whatever answers at that address, so prefer rtsps:// and trusted networks. HTTPS SOAP and Media2-only devices are unsupported. HDMI capture devices use their operating system video driver. CSI cameras must have an accessible video device with a supported driver. Capturefab does not implement libcamera-only pipelines or proprietary camera tethering protocols. capturefab compatibility MODEL gives connection guidance. It does not certify camera compatibility. Camera types and measurement data The interface adapts to area-scan, line-scan, depth, microscope, thermal and document-scanner profiles. A profile identifies available control families. It does not prove physical camera compatibility or writable access. Examine the current feature list and limits before you change a setting. Expand Camera details in Features to read acquisition guidance and the evidence used to detect the camera type. Line-scan previews show recent rows, with gaps for skipped blocks. Captures save individual acquired blocks. Depth and thermal previews show colors for an automatic raw-value range. These colors do not apply measurement calibration. Select Sensor pixels to return to the ordinary preview. For depth or temperature measurements, use --format raw . Separately retain dimensions, pixel format, selected component, units, scale, offset and calibration features. Raw files preserve acquired bytes without that metadata. PNG, JPEG, PGM, PPM and forwarded video are 8-bit display outputs. Depth sources must have a compatible single-component stream. Multipart, GenDC and point-cloud payloads are unsupported. Use sim:line , sim:depth , sim:microscope or sim:thermal to try the specialized controls without camera hardware. See Camera compatibility for profile and transport limits.

documents.title: Test with simulated cameras and replay files
documents.summary: Use generated images or recorded files to learn the controls and test a capture workflow without camera hardware.
documents.body: Test with simulated cameras and replay files Use generated images or recorded files to learn the controls and test a capture workflow without camera hardware. Enter sim:0 for a moving pattern. Use sim:line , sim:depth , sim:microscope or sim:thermal to try the related controls. Replay local files Put test images or video files in a folder. Enter sim:replay:/absolute/path/to/folder in the camera address field. Start live view or save a capture. A replay source can also be one file. Folder replay reads only the top level and ignores symlinks. It sorts filenames in case-sensitive order and loops the selected files. Use names such as 0001.png to control that order. Reconnect after changing the folder contents. Local replay starts at 640 × 480 RGB8 and 30 fps. Stop acquisition before changing width, height or frame rate. Images retain their proportions, with black padding where necessary. FFmpeg decodes the files. capturefab --camera 'sim:replay:/data/test-images' capture -n 10 -o replay capturefab simulate presets capturefab simulate run --preset onvif --source ./test-images --duration 5m Host a virtual network camera simulate run hosts a GigE Vision, RTSP or ONVIF test camera. The command prints its connection addresses. It runs until you push Ctrl+C or its duration expires. Virtual camera presets Preset Default output gige 640 × 480 RGB8 at 30 fps over GigE Vision vision 640 × 480 RGB8 at 60 fps over GigE Vision rtsp 1920 × 1080 H.264 at 30 fps and 4 Mbit/s onvif 1280 × 720 H.264 at 15 fps and 2 Mbit/s, with ONVIF discovery Listeners use loopback by default. For another computer, set --bind to a reachable local address. With --bind 0.0.0.0 , also set --advertise LAN_IP . The test server has no authentication. Use a trusted test network. The simulation implements a subset of each protocol. It does not simulate USB3 Vision, PTZ, audio or motion events. See the simulation command reference and integration examples .

documents.title: Open cameras from Home Assistant, Frigate, go2rtc and UniFi Protect
documents.summary: Save a Home Assistant, Frigate, go2rtc or UniFi Protect server as a hub. Its cameras then appear on the camera picker and open as hub:NAME/CAMERA .
documents.body: Connect & examine Open cameras from Home Assistant, Frigate, go2rtc and UniFi Protect Save a Home Assistant, Frigate, go2rtc or UniFi Protect server as a hub. Its cameras then appear on the camera picker and open as hub:NAME/CAMERA . Save the hub with a capturefab hub add-… command. The command makes sure that the server replies and accepts the secret. In the app, run discovery. Cameras on saved hubs appear after the local cameras. Select a hub camera to connect it. You can also enter its hub:NAME/CAMERA ID in the address field. Start the stream, capture or record as with other cameras. # Home Assistant: a long-lived access token from Profile > Security capturefab hub add-home-assistant home --url http://homeassistant.local:8123 \ --secret-stdin < token.txt capturefab hub add-frigate nvr --url http://nvr.local:5000 capturefab hub add-go2rtc streams --url http://go2rtc.local:1984 # UniFi Protect: an API key from Settings > Control Plane > Integrations capturefab hub add-unifi-protect protect --url https://192.168.1.1 \ --secret-stdin --accept-certificate < api-key.txt capturefab hub list capturefab hub cameras home capturefab hub test home capturefab --camera 'hub:home/camera.front_door' capture -o front.png capturefab --camera 'hub:home/camera.porch?stream=snapshot&fps=0.5' \ capture --interval 1m -n 60 -o porch Hub cameras Hub Camera ID Streams (auto first) Home Assistant hub:NAME/camera.ENTITY mjpeg , snapshot Frigate hub:NAME/CAMERA , with the camera name rtsp (the Frigate restream), snapshot ; also mjpeg go2rtc hub:NAME/STREAM rtsp , snapshot ; also mjpeg for JPEG sources UniFi Protect hub:NAME/CAMERA_ID , with 24 hexadecimal digits snapshot stream=auto is the default. It tries the streams in table order and keeps the first that supplies a frame. To select a stream, add ?stream=mjpeg , ?stream=snapshot or ?stream=rtsp . With stream=snapshot , fps sets images per second. Home Assistant and go2rtc accept 0.01–2; Frigate accepts 0.01–5; UniFi Protect accepts 0.01–1. Frigate MJPEG accepts a whole fps from 1 to 10. Put selectors in quotation marks because shells interpret ? and & . In CAMERA, percent-encode characters outside A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ as %XX . hub cameras returns correctly formed IDs. Server addresses and secrets Home Assistant uses a long-lived access token from Profile > Security . Use a dedicated user without administrator access. The token grants that user's access. Frigate uses http://HOST:5000 without a user, or https://HOST:8971 with --user and a password. For go2rtc, provide --user and a password when its API uses them. UniFi Protect uses https://CONSOLE . Create its API key in Settings > Control Plane > Integrations . --secret-stdin reads the secret into the operating system keychain. The desktop, serve and CLI can use that saved secret. --secret-env CAPTUREFAB_HUB_NAME saves only an environment variable's name. The process that opens or lists cameras reads its value. For session commands, that process is the desktop or serve ; otherwise it is the CLI. A desktop started from the Dock, Finder or Start menu does not inherit shell variables. Use --secret-stdin for that desktop. Builds without keychain support accept only --secret-env . Never put secrets in command arguments. The saved hubs.json file in the state directory contains no secrets. Adding a hub with an existing name replaces it. Without a secret option, a replacement for the same server keeps its saved keychain secret. If the server refuses a secret, discovery stops using that hub. A successful hub test NAME or explicit camera connection clears this state. Adding the hub again also clears it. Home Assistant can block an address after repeated failed logins when IP banning is enabled. hub remove NAME --forget-secret removes both the hub and its keychain secret. Certificates For https:// hubs, Capturefab trusts operating system certificates. UniFi consoles and Frigate port 8971 usually have self-signed certificates. --accept-certificate trusts the certificate presented now and prints its fingerprint. Confirm the fingerprint with the server administrator. --certificate SHA256:… pins a known fingerprint. --tls-server-name NAME compares a trusted certificate against NAME when the URL uses an IP address. Use only one certificate option. If a pinned certificate changes, the camera stops. Over http:// , secrets travel without encryption. Limits Hub camera settings are read-only. Change them in the hub. Capturefab decodes JPEG, PNG and MJPEG in the camera worker. It uses FFmpeg for RTSP restreams, which open without a password. Each stream attempt allows at least 12 seconds for its first frame, or 15 seconds for RTSP. --timeout-ms can increase that allowance. API calls and fallback attempts can extend total connection time. Home Assistant MJPEG sends no new frame while the image stays unchanged. Use stream=snapshot for static scenes and timelapses. Streams reconnect automatically after network failure. A refused secret or certificate stops acquisition. HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY have no effect. serve --listen refuses hub cameras for browser and HTTP clients unless started with --allow-hubs . Exit code 1 indicates a refused secret or certificate; 2 indicates invalid names, URLs, flags or selectors. Exit code 3 indicates an unavailable hub or camera; 4 indicates a timeout. Exit code 5 indicates missing hub or keychain build support. Compatibility with specific hub versions and cameras has not been validated.

documents.title: Scan documents
documents.summary: Scanners use the same capture, preview, destination, schedule and storage tools. Each capture requests one page.
documents.body: Connect & examine Scan documents Scanners use the same capture, preview, destination, schedule and storage tools. Each capture requests one page. Discover a scanner. Connect its full ID. Open Features . Select Scan resolution , Scan mode and Scan source . Open Capture . Select Scan & save . A connection or acquisition start does not scan a page. Scanner controls Feature Values Default ScanResolution 75–600 dpi 150 ScanMode Color , Gray , Lineart Color ScanSource Default , Flatbed , Feeder Default, leaving the driver’s source unchanged capturefab scanners --json # Replace DEVICE with the full returned scanner ID capturefab --camera 'scanner:sane:DEVICE' --timeout-ms 60000 capture \ --set ScanResolution=300 --set ScanMode=Gray --set ScanSource=Feeder \ -n 5 -o pages Linux uses the installed SANE scanimage and backends. CAPTUREFAB_SCANIMAGE sets the executable path. Windows uses a WIA driver through Windows PowerShell. macOS uses an included ImageCaptureCore helper and a compatible driver. Drivers can reject unsupported settings. Capturefab does not select a different mode after a rejection. Use Default if a SANE driver has source names other than Flatbed or Automatic Document Feeder. The GUI scanner timeout defaults to 60 seconds. For CLI scans, use --timeout-ms 60000 . A timeout, stop or disconnect terminates acquisition. A capture with several pages saves a separate image for each page. Samples use 8-bit RGB or grayscale, with a 128 MiB page limit. Scanner sources do not support PDF assembly, OCR, stream forwarding or camera auto exposure. Physical scanner compatibility has not been validated.

documents.title: Examine and change camera features
documents.summary: The Features panel reads the camera’s current feature map. It shows values, access permissions, choices, limits and units.
documents.body: Connect & examine Examine and change camera features The Features panel reads the camera’s current feature map. It shows values, access permissions, choices, limits and units. Quick controls keep common settings in view. Expand a feature group or search to reveal additional controls. Select a connected camera. Open Features . Use Quick controls , expand a feature group, or search by feature name, display label or description. Edit a numeric or text value. Push Enter or select Apply . Read back the accepted value. Choice menus and checkboxes apply changes immediately. A camera can round a value to its supported increment. A rejected write shows its reason beside the field. Less common controls appear in Image, Acquisition, Device, Transport and Other groups. Each group shows its feature count. Search reveals matching controls across all groups, including closed groups. Clear the search to return to Quick controls and your expanded groups. Names and available features depend on the source. Point to a label to see its feature name and description. For settings locked during acquisition, the Locked while streaming notice provides a Stop button. capturefab --camera sim:0 features --filter Exposure capturefab --camera sim:0 get Width Height PixelFormat ExposureTime capturefab --camera sim:0 set ExposureTime=5000 Gain=0 # A camera command, when the device exposes it capturefab --session bench execute TriggerSoftware CLI assignments run in the specified order. A later failure does not reverse earlier successful writes. Examine the features before a write. Read back important values after a write. A manual edit to an Auto-managed feature changes that camera to manual mode. Use Undo and Redo for acknowledged, reversible settings.

documents.title: Tune auto exposure and frame rate
documents.summary: Enable Auto for one camera. Select the balance between image quality and frame rate. Cameras start in manual mode.
documents.body: Connect & examine Tune auto exposure and frame rate Enable Auto for one camera. Select the balance between image quality and frame rate. Cameras start in manual mode. In Features , select Auto on the Exposure card. Move the slider toward Quality for longer exposure with less gain. Move it toward Frame rate for shorter exposure with more gain. The default balance is 0.5, at the midpoint. Auto uses the camera’s automatic exposure, gain and white balance controls when available. Otherwise, Capturefab adjusts exposure and gain. If link capacity permits, Auto can increase frame-rate or GigE throughput limits. It reduces these values if packet loss occurs. Expand Auto changes to see each change and its reason. Stable and Limited are settled states. Waiting means that acquisition is stopped. capturefab --session bench auto --balance quality capturefab --session bench auto --balance 0.5 capturefab --session bench status --json capturefab --session bench manual capturefab --session bench manual --revert capturefab --camera sim:0 capture --auto --balance 0.25 -o tuned.png manual disables camera auto functions and keeps their current values. manual --revert restores the settings that Auto changed. Disconnect, direct-command exit and session exit also restore those settings where possible. In a persistent session, capture --auto keeps Auto enabled after capture. For capture --auto , Capturefab applies repeated --set assignments first. It waits for exposure to settle for half the transport timeout, with a maximum wait of 3 seconds. It can save a frame before exposure settles. Examine result.auto.state in the JSON result. An image camera with suitable controls is necessary for auto exposure. It can support microscopes with those controls. Line-scan, depth, thermal and document-scanner sources do not support generic auto exposure. Configure their timing or measurement controls directly.

documents.title: Preview, zoom and compare cameras
documents.summary: Each camera has its own window. Arrange windows side by side to compare live cameras.
documents.body: Connect & examine Preview, zoom and compare cameras Each camera has its own window. Arrange windows side by side to compare live cameras. Push ⌘N / Ctrl+N to connect another source in a new window. Each camera acquires independently, and closing one window does not stop another camera’s stream. Fit centers the entire frame in the available area. Use ⌘0 on macOS or Ctrl+0 elsewhere. Actual pixels shows the image at 1:1 with ⌥⌘0 or Ctrl+Alt+0 . Zoom in / out uses ⌘+ / ⌘− or Ctrl+= / Ctrl+− . Image only hides workspace panels. Push F when no field has focus, then push it again to return. The live preview uses the latest frame when the display cannot keep up. Preview scale does not change saved resolution. A fitted preview converts only enough pixels for its display size. Actual pixels and closer zooms show every pixel. In efficiency mode, a fitted preview keeps at most 1280 pixels on its long side. Reduced previews sample pixels instead of averaging them. A session supports 16 connected cameras by default. CAPTUREFAB_MAX_CAMERAS accepts 1–64. If the preview fails, open the camera’s Activity details. Troubleshooting covers frame timeouts, graphics fallback and transport diagnostics.

documents.title: Read the histogram and focus scores
documents.summary: Use the histogram to examine shadows and highlights. Use the focus region to compare image sharpness as you adjust the lens.
documents.body: Connect & examine Read the histogram and focus scores Use the histogram to examine shadows and highlights. Use the focus region to compare image sharpness as you adjust the lens. The histogram measures intensity and clipping. The focus card measures sharpness in the outlined region. It compares the current score with the observed peak. Histogram Push H outside an input field to show the Histogram. It displays Mean intensity, Shadows at black and Highlights with a saturated channel. Use these measurements to guide exposure and gain settings. The histogram does not change settings. For a camera with writable exposure or gain, select Shadows or Highlights to open that control in Features. During camera Auto exposure, the control opens the camera's Auto setting. While streaming, the histogram updates five times per second and the focus score up to 15 times per second. Focus region Push R outside an input field to show the focus region and score. Position the region over useful image detail. Adjust the region size. Choose a focus measure ( Edges , Strong edges , Texture or Contrast ) in the Focus card's chooser. Adjust the lens to increase the score. Compare the trend and % of peak with similar light and scene content. After a scene change, select Reset peak (the reset button on the Focus card) before a new adjustment. Focus measures Measure What it measures Edges (Laplacian) Variance of the Laplacian; responds to fine edges. Strong edges (Tenengrad) Squared Sobel gradient; useful on strong edges and in noise. Texture (Brenner) Squared differences two pixels apart; favors fine texture. Contrast (Variance) Normalized intensity variance; a contrast measure, gentle on noise. The score compares image sharpness. It is not a lens calibration or an autofocus command. Subject, light, gain and focus-region changes can change the score independently of lens focus.

documents.title: Capture images and sequences
documents.summary: Save one frame to a file. Save several frames to a directory or a sequence with a {frame} filename template.
documents.body: Capture & save Capture images and sequences Save one frame to a file. Save several frames to a directory or a sequence with a {frame} filename template. Ordinary captures start with the manual controls. Timeout and scheduling, storage limits and shell access stay in labeled sections below them. Open Capture for the selected camera. Select a destination in Save to . Choose how files are named in File names , and where in Folder . To enter a file, folder or template, choose Custom pattern… . Set Frames and Format . Select Capture & save . Read the saved path or error below the button. The default output is ~/Capturefab/{date}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.png . Each capture gets a new name. Camera and time omits the dated folder. Numbered uses capture-{seq} names. A manually entered template keeps its field open. Next file shows the next path in the selected folder. Select Show in Finder to open the last capture's folder. Windows calls this Show in Explorer ; Linux uses Show in folder . Capture All in the toolbar saves one frame from each connected camera. Expand Capture options to change the transport timeout. Use Capture on a schedule for delayed or interval captures. Storage & retention and Shell & agents reveal their setup when you need it. capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o frame.png capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -n 10 -o frames capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -n 10 -o 'run-{frame}.png' capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'line1/{date}/{camera}-{seq}.png' capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o frame.jpg capturefab --camera sim:0 capture --set Width=640 --set Height=480 -o configured.png # One binary image to stdout; do not combine with --json capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o - --format ppm > frame.ppm Image formats Format Use png Default lossless 8-bit output: one gray channel for monochrome cameras, RGB for color and Bayer. Carries tags and camera settings. jpeg / jpg Lossy still images at quality 90; the JPEG build feature is necessary. Carries tags and camera settings. raw Preserve frame bytes when image conversion is unsupported or unnecessary. pgm Portable grayscale output. ppm Portable RGB output. Capturefab selects the image format from the extension of a single filename or template. It recognizes .png , .jpg , .jpeg , .raw , .pgm and .ppm . Directory sequences, outputs without an extension and stdout default to PNG. --format overrides this selection. With an unknown extension, specify the format. Local CLI and RPC output paths use the directory of the terminal that sends the command. This also applies when the GUI starts from another directory. With --destination NAME , output names are relative to that saved destination. --timeout-ms sets the per-frame transport timeout from 1 to 60,000 ms. Its default is 2,000 ms. --count accepts 1–100,000 frames. Capturefab does not overwrite existing output files. Use a {seq} template or --on-exists number to get a new name each time. See File names and tags . For delayed and repeated captures, see Scheduled captures .

documents.title: Name files and tag captures
documents.summary: Use a template to give each capture and recording a new file name. Add tags that tell the analysis what each file shows.
documents.body: Capture & save Name files and tag captures Use a template to give each capture and recording a new file name. Add tags that tell the analysis what each file shows. Output placeholders Placeholder Value {camera} Model and serial number, with only A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - ; a maximum of 64 bytes. It never contains the address. {date} YYYY-MM-DD {time} HHMMSS {datetime} YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS {seq} The next free number for that folder and pattern, with 4 or more digits. {frame} The frame number in a multi-frame capture, with 6 digits. {tag:KEY} The capture tag KEY , such as {tag:label} , made into one safe folder or file name. capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'line1/{date}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.png' capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o shot.png --on-exists number capturefab --camera sim:0 record -o 'video/{camera}-{seq}.mp4' --duration 30s capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'qa/{camera}-{seq}.png' \ --context line=L1 --context station=S2 --context part=A-100 capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'dataset/{tag:label}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.png' \ --context label=defect Times use the local clock when Capturefab requests the frame. Use {seq} only once and only in the file name. Do not put a digit, a time placeholder or a tag directly after {seq} . Other names in braces cause a usage error. {tag:KEY} sorts captures into a folder per class or condition, each with its own {seq} numbers. Capturefab trims the value, replaces / \ < > : " | ? * with _ , removes trailing dots and spaces, adds _ before a leading dot or a Windows device name such as CON , and keeps at most 128 bytes. An empty or missing tag is a usage error that names the tag. A schedule keeps the tags it was created with; changing a tag later does not move its files. Capturefab never overwrites a file. Without {seq} , an existing name causes an error. --on-exists number adds -0001 , -0002 and the subsequent numbers to the name. A directory output continues after its highest frame-NNNNNN number. A name ending in / is always a folder, and a name without an extension gets the format's, such as .png . A multi-frame template must contain {frame} or {seq} , or use --on-exists number . Several frames sent to one image name, such as -n 3 -o shot.jpg , are a usage error that suggests -o 'shot-{seq}.jpg' or -o shot/ . An explicit --format must match the image extension in the name. The desktop app always adds a number to an existing name. Its default recording output is ~/Capturefab/{date}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.mp4 . Read the saved names in result.files and result.frames[].file . A recording result gives the file in path . Capture tags In Capture , expand Capture tags . Enter Label , Line , Station , Part , Lot and Note as necessary. The app sends them with each capture and recording as the context keys label , line , station , part , lot and note . Choose File names › One folder per label to save each Label, such as good or defect , in its own folder; Next file asks for a Label while it is empty. An open dataset keeps them in each row. Without a dataset, the section says so and links to Dataset . From the CLI, use --context KEY=VALUE once for each tag. A key starts with a lowercase letter and contains a maximum of 32 lowercase letters, digits and underscores. A capture accepts a maximum of 16 tags, with 256 bytes for each value. Metadata in saved images Each saved PNG and JPEG records where it came from, with or without a dataset. PNG files hold compact JSON in an iTXt chunk named capturefab , and the tags as key=value; … in the standard Description . JPEG files hold the same JSON in a comment (COM) segment. The JSON has the frame ID, timestamps, size, pixel format name, camera vendor and model, the tags under context , and under settings the current values of acquisition features such as ExposureTime , Gain and AcquisitionFrameRate when the camera has them. It never contains a serial number, address or source URL. Tags, including note , travel with the file, so leave out anything you would not share with it. Raw, PGM and PPM files have no metadata.

documents.title: Schedule captures and timelapses
documents.summary: Start capture later or capture at intervals. The session shows job progress and the next frame time. You can cancel pending or active jobs.
documents.body: Capture & save Schedule captures and timelapses Start capture later or capture at intervals. The session shows job progress and the next frame time. You can cancel pending or active jobs. In Capture options, enable scheduling to reveal the delay and interval. This example schedules one frame after 5 seconds. Frame interval controls the spacing in a sequence. In Capture, set the output, frame count and format. Expand Capture options and enable Capture on a schedule . Enter Start after and Frame interval in seconds. Select Schedule capture . Scheduled jobs shows progress. Use its Stop button to cancel pending or active work. # Direct commands wait for their job to finish capturefab --direct --camera sim:0 capture --delay 30s -o later.png capturefab --direct --camera sim:0 capture --interval 10s -n 360 -o timelapse # Existing sessions return a job ID capturefab --session bench capture --delay 5s --interval 1m -n 60 -o timed-frames capturefab --session bench jobs --json capturefab --session bench cancel 1 # Use a future timestamp with an explicit timezone capturefab --session bench capture --at 2026-12-01T09:00:00-05:00 \ --interval 1m -n 100 -o morning Use --at or --delay to set the start time. Durations accept ms , s , m , h , d , or plain seconds. The frame count limits a timelapse. Each frame acquisition has its own transport timeout. Durations and timestamp fractions must resolve to whole milliseconds. 1.001s is valid; 1.1ms is invalid. All scheduled frames must occur within 10 years. A past timestamp starts capture immediately. A zero RPC interval captures consecutive frames. Two active jobs on one camera cannot share a fixed filename or {frame} -only template. They can share a directory, a {seq} template or numbered output. Keep the GUI, headless session or direct command active. Schedules end when its process exits. The stop command stops acquisition and cancels pending capture jobs on that camera. A stopped or failed job stays visible with its progress and error. Scheduled frames save in the background while preview, recording and forwarding continue. The save queue holds two frames. If it is full when a shot arrives, the job skips that shot and reschedules it for a later interval. A briefly busy or slow disk also moves the shot to the next interval. The job card counts skipped and retried shots. A full disk or another save error stops the job.

documents.title: Catalog and export datasets
documents.summary: Catalog saved images, recordings and notes in one DuckDB file. Export their metadata, and optionally the images, for analysis and training.
documents.body: Capture & save Catalog and export datasets Catalog saved images, recordings and notes in one DuckDB file. Export their metadata, and optionally the images, for analysis and training. In Capture , expand Dataset . Select New… or Open… , or keep Catalog captures automatically on. Capture and record as usual. Keep Include captured images on to copy the images into the export, then select Export… and select a folder. Open the README.md that the app shows after the export. The automatic dataset is ~/Capturefab/capturefab.duckdb . The app opens the same dataset at the next start. The section summary shows the file name and the number of captures and recordings. Use Show in Finder to find the file. Use Close before you copy it. capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'line1/{camera}-{seq}.png' --dataset plant.duckdb capturefab --session line1 dataset open plant.duckdb capturefab --session line1 dataset note "shift B start" --context line=L1 capturefab --session line1 dataset status capturefab --session line1 dataset query \ "SELECT camera_id, path, wall_ms FROM captures LIMIT 20" capturefab --session line1 dataset export -o exports/shift-b capturefab --session line1 dataset export -o exports/shift-b-images --media images --group-by part capturefab --session line1 dataset close # A dataset that no session holds capturefab dataset query --file plant.duckdb "SELECT count(*) FROM captures" capturefab dataset export --file plant.duckdb -o exports/csv-only --format csv The same workflow without a session, as three commands. The export folder holds the tables, manifest.json and README.md ; the images stay in parts/ . # Capture 3 tagged images, 500 ms apart, into a catalog capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -n 3 --interval 500ms --context part=A-100 --dataset parts.duckdb -o 'parts/{camera}-{seq}.png' # Query the catalog with SQL capturefab dataset query --file parts.duckdb "SELECT path, wall_ms, context FROM captures" # Export Parquet and CSV tables with manifest.json and README.md capturefab dataset export --file parts.duckdb -o export Dataset tables Table Content captures One row for each saved image: time, camera, frame data, path, SHA-256, destination and tags. recordings One row for each finished local recording. events Notes, dataset open and close, and capture errors. Each *_ms column is UTC Unix milliseconds from the computer clock. The context column contains JSON text. A query accepts one read-only SELECT or WITH statement. It returns a maximum of 10,000 rows and stops after 30 seconds. A query cannot read or write other files. An export writes into a new folder; an existing folder is refused. Default formats are Parquet and CSV. JSON and JSONL are also available. The export includes manifest.json and README.md . The README explains timestamps, lists files and provides loading examples and a summary for AI tools. By default, images and videos stay at the paths recorded in the tables. --media images copies the captured images into images/ in the export, and --media all also copies recordings into videos/ . With --tables , only files from the listed tables are copied. --group-by KEY puts them in one folder per value of that tag, such as images/A-100/ , with untagged files in images/_unlabeled/ . media.csv lists each copy's relative export_path , SHA-256 and group and joins to the tables on table and id , so you can move or zip the folder. Copies count against the storage budget and never overwrite. Capturefab checks each copy against the cataloged SHA-256 and skips files that are missing or changed; manifest.json lists them. A session keeps the dataset file open. To read the file from another command, use --session NAME . With --file , a held file causes exit code 3. The default size limit is 8 GiB. Writes stop with exit code 6 when less than 512 MiB of disk space is free. An export that does not fit the storage budget stops before it writes a file.

documents.title: Save to folders and drives
documents.summary: Save a folder with a name, then select it for images, scheduled captures and local recordings. You can choose your disk, a removable drive or a mounted network drive.
documents.body: Capture & save Save to folders and drives Save a folder with a name, then select it for images, scheduled captures and local recordings. You can choose your disk, a removable drive or a mounted network drive. Open Manage… beside Save to in Capture or Video. Select Add folder… and choose the folder. Enter a destination name. Select Test to check access, then Save . Select the saved destination in Save to . Choose how files are named in File names . Custom pattern… is relative to the selected folder. capturefab volumes --json capturefab destination add-folder archive '/path/to/captures' capturefab destination list --json capturefab destination test archive capturefab --camera sim:0 capture --destination archive -o run-1 -n 10 Mounted drives appear as shortcuts in the destination selector. If an external drive is absent, Capturefab refuses to write under its unmounted mount point. Removing a destination does not remove files. Upgrade saved destinations Only folder destinations appear in this version. Saved destinations of other kinds from earlier versions are ignored. Existing folder destinations and their files remain available. To save on network storage, mount it with your operating system first. Then add its mounted folder as a destination.

documents.title: Set storage budgets and retention
documents.summary: Capturefab tracks its output files across folders and processes. The initial shared storage limit is 10 GiB and 10,000 files.
documents.body: Capture & save Set storage budgets and retention Capturefab tracks its output files across folders and processes. The initial shared storage limit is 10 GiB and 10,000 files. Recover retained camera catalogs Retained camera catalog workspaces remain charged to storage until explicitly removed. Recovery refuses a running owner. Save a copy into a new folder to preserve its database and WAL together. capturefab storage task-data list --json capturefab storage task-data copy RESERVATION_ID recovered-catalog --json # Only after approving deletion of this exact workspace: capturefab storage task-data remove RESERVATION_ID --confirmed-by-user --json Use the inventory's reservation ID. Copies use additional storage budget; keep task.duckdb.wal beside task.duckdb . Changed directories, extra hard links or uncertain shutdown keep their reservation charged. Inspect partial output before retrying a failed copy. Open Storage & retention in Capture, or in Video with Record to file selected. Its closed summary shows the current budget. Use up to limits storage bytes. Keep at most limits file count. When full selects whether Capturefab stops or deletes the oldest eligible files. With deletion enabled, Delete captures older than a set age and Older than add an age limit. An app-wide policy can be stricter. capturefab storage --json capturefab storage configure --max-space 2GiB --max-files 1000 --on-full stop capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -n 100 -o frames --max-space 1GiB # Explicitly allow deletion of verified Capturefab-owned files capturefab --camera sim:0 capture --interval 1m -n 10000 -o history \ --max-space 1GiB --delete-oldest --max-age 7d # Remove a saved age limit capturefab storage configure --no-max-age storage configure saves the global policy for later runs. Per-command limits can lower this limit. Active recording reservations use the same budget. Each video file also has a size limit, initially 512 MiB. A recording stops at that limit and keeps the video written so far. The budget covers Capturefab captures and recordings, not unrelated files. The default stop policy reports storage_full , with exit code 6. --delete-oldest permits deletion of completed Capturefab files only if their identity and SHA-256 still match. Retention protects user files, modified captures, replacements and active recordings. Capturefab applies age retention when it allocates new captures. Processes of one user share the storage ledger and budget in the state directory, which survives reboots. A different CAPTUREFAB_SESSION_DIR uses a separate ledger. If a tracked file is missing, Capturefab releases its recorded usage. After a crash, the operating system releases locks so Capturefab can reconcile interrupted reservations.

documents.title: Find saved paths and examine Activity
documents.summary: Read the saved path below the capture button. Open Activity to see command history and full error details.
documents.body: Capture & save Find saved paths and examine Activity Read the saved path below the capture button. Open Activity to see command history and full error details. After a successful capture, the line below Capture & save shows the saved filename or sequence folder. It also shows the named destination, if used. Put the pointer on the line to see the path. Use the copy button to copy it. For scheduled captures, examine the path and frame count in Scheduled jobs . Open Activity from the bottom toolbar or View menu, or push ⌘J / Ctrl+J . In a narrow preview, the toolbar keeps its waveform icon and shows the label on hover. Events show participant commands, results, warnings and errors across all cameras. Select Details on an error notice to read its full message. Desktop, browser, CLI, RPC and workflow commands appear in Activity . Each entry has an actor, camera, source and state: queued, running, succeeded or failed. Output summaries and errors remain after selection changes or camera disconnection. Sequences show their file count and sample paths. status --json includes this history in result.activity and its revision in result.activity_revision . Read-only observations and authenticated session discovery do not add entries. Use --actor NAME --actor-kind agent to identify an automation agent. Use --actor-kind human to identify a person. CAPTUREFAB_ACTOR and CAPTUREFAB_ACTOR_KIND supply defaults. Actor metadata provides display attribution. It does not authenticate a participant. capturefab --session bench --actor capture-agent --actor-kind agent connect sim:0 --json capturefab --session bench --actor capture-agent --actor-kind agent --camera sim:0 capture -o 'shot-{seq}.png' --json Background work shows toolbar progress and an Activity indicator for new actions. Keyboard focus and open panels stay in place. Captures update the saved path. Streams, forwarding and scheduled jobs use shared session state. Feature values update without a change to your text drafts. Activity keeps the latest 200 completed entries plus active commands and schedules for the session lifetime. Each scheduled job keeps its actor, status, saved frame count, last file and errors until completion or cancellation. Forwarding command success confirms encoder startup. Examine camera status to confirm that forwarding continues. Persons and agents can capture from the same camera. Commands for one camera run in order. Separate cameras work independently, and overlapping scheduled jobs share acquisition. Browser tabs have separate identities and editable names. The default actor kind is human . For local activity, run capturefab --session NAME activity --json . Use its revision in later activity --after REV --wait 20s --json calls. Each response contains {revision,activity} and bypasses capture queues. The browser waits for shared changes with GET /api/activity?after=REV&timeout_ms=20000 . Local IPC permits eight waiting observers. HTTP permits 32 waiting observers alongside command connections. Use Copy log to copy the error into a bug report. Activity records session feedback. The storage ledger tracks Capturefab files and disk usage. capturefab --session bench status --json capturefab --session bench jobs --json capturefab storage --json capturefab storage --json

documents.title: Undo and redo changes
documents.summary: Undo desktop edits and acknowledged, reversible camera changes. Each connected camera shares its change history with session clients.
documents.body: Capture & save Undo and redo changes Undo desktop edits and acknowledged, reversible camera changes. Each connected camera shares its change history with session clients. The destination manager also offers Undo and Redo. This macOS view shows the shortcuts beside each action; in the editor, each button’s tooltip shows its shortcut. Redo is disabled until you undo a change. Select Undo or Redo in the Edit menu. The bottom toolbar also shows them when there is enough room. On macOS, use ⌘Z or ⇧⌘Z . Elsewhere, use Ctrl+Z or Ctrl+Shift+Z . Outside macOS, Ctrl+Y also applies Redo. Continuous edits form one change. A new change clears Redo. capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 history --json capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 undo --json capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 redo --json Camera history includes reversible feature writes, auto/manual mode changes and stream changes. status.history and cameras[].history show the next Undo and Redo labels, or null . History is limited and lasts for the camera connection. Replay examines the camera state. A conflict or failed replay keeps the entry for inspection. Camera history cannot reverse capture files, recordings, schedules, connections, arbitrary camera commands or raw memory writes. It also excludes a stream stop with active schedules or forwarding. Examine the next label before you undo another participant’s change.

documents.title: Save and restore camera setups
documents.summary: Save a tuned camera's settings by name, then restore them later after a preview of what changes. A restore is one change that Undo reverts.
documents.body: Capture & save Save and restore camera setups Save a tuned camera's settings by name, then restore them later after a preview of what changes. A restore is one change that Undo reverts. Tune the camera, then select Camera › Save Setup… , or Save setup… above the Features list. Enter a name, such as line-2-mono , and an optional note. The sheet lists the settings a setup leaves out, such as values a camera auto mode sets. Later, select Camera › Restore Setup… and choose the setup. Review Changes , Not applied and any note about the stream, then select Restore . Settings marked Changes camera behavior , such as trigger and I/O line settings, need a second click on Confirm Restore . A setup from another camera model shows a warning, and restores only after you select Apply to this different camera model . Changing the image size or pixel format stops and restarts a running stream once; this is refused while the camera records, forwards or runs scheduled captures. capturefab --camera sim:0 setup save bench --note "Ring light at 60%" capturefab setup list capturefab --session bench setup diff bench capturefab --session bench setup apply bench capturefab --session bench undo capturefab setup show bench --json > bench.json capturefab setup import bench.json --name bench-copy A setup holds each writable setting at the selected bank, and every bank of the gain, black level, white balance, trigger, line, user output, counter and timer selectors. It never holds network, user-set or file settings, commands, stream state, capture settings, credentials or addresses, and it never changes the camera's own user sets. Restoring writes image size and format first, turns triggers and output lines on only after their sources, retries values an earlier write unlocks or makes available, and checks every saved value; if one does not take, every value is put back. The preview also shows when restoring starts or stops auto exposure. On the command line, setup apply asks for --yes before disruptive changes, --allow-other-model for another model and --strict refuses any value the camera cannot take, also with --dry-run ; setup diff previews another model with a warning. Workflows restore a setup with the step {"camera":"sim:0","command":{"op":"apply_setup","name":"bench"}} . Setups are kept in setups/ in the state folder; setup list shows where. Back them up with setup show NAME --json .

documents.title: Record bounded video files
documents.summary: Select Record on the toolbar to record the selected camera to a local file. The Video panel also publishes a stream. A shared storage budget and a file-size limit control recording output.
documents.body: Record & automate Record bounded video files Select Record on the toolbar to record the selected camera to a local file. The Video panel also publishes a stream. A shared storage budget and a file-size limit control recording output. Select Record , or push ⇧⌘R on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+R elsewhere. The toolbar shows elapsed time. Select Stop or push the same keys to finish the file. The File menu also has Start Recording and Stop Recording . The default file is ~/Capturefab/{date}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.mp4 . Camera › Record All Cameras records each camera to a separate file. The recording card includes a button to show its file in the folder. Open Video and keep Record to file selected. To change the output, expand Location & name . Select a destination in Save to . Enter a filename or template, such as clip-{seq}.mkv , in File . For saved destinations, this field is Recording file name in destination . Optionally, expand Video settings to set Codec , Frame rate , Bitrate , Encoder or Maximum file . Select Start recording . When saving to this computer, Saves as under it shows the next file's path. When you have sufficient footage, select Stop recording to finish the file. # record is an alias of forward capturefab --camera sim:0 record -o clip.mkv --duration 30s \ --codec h264 --encoder auto --fps 30 --bitrate 4M --max-file-size 512MiB # A template gives each recording a new name capturefab --camera sim:0 record -o 'video/{camera}-{seq}.mp4' --duration 30s --context line=L1 # A persistent session records until stopped capturefab --session bench record -o clip.mp4 --destination archive capturefab --session bench stop-forward Local .mkv , fragmented .mp4 / .mov , .ts and suitable .webm files use a writer with a size limit. Select a codec that the container supports. --duration works with temporary workers and persistent sessions. The CLI stays active until the deadline or Ctrl-C, then stops the encoder. Without a duration, a session command returns immediately and records until stop-forward . A temporary worker records until Ctrl-C. Defaults are H.264, 30 fps, bitrate 4M and a maximum file size of 512 MiB. Encoder auto tries available hardware, then software. Enter an FFmpeg encoder name to select an encoder directly. Use doctor and ffmpeg to examine the computer and build.

documents.title: Forward a stream to a recorder
documents.summary: Send frames to an RTSP, SRT, RTMP, UDP or HTTP destination. Start the receiver or recording server before you send the stream.
documents.body: Record & automate Forward a stream to a recorder Send frames to an RTSP, SRT, RTMP, UDP or HTTP destination. Start the receiver or recording server before you send the stream. The Video panel publishes to a stream URL or records to a file. Video settings sums up the codec, frame rate and bitrate, and reveals them with the encoder choice and maximum local file size. In Video , select Forward to URL and enter the receiver address in Stream URL . To change the codec, frame rate, bitrate or encoder, expand Video settings . Select Start forwarding . The active stream card shows its destination and a stop control. Form edits do not change an active stream. capturefab --camera sim:0 forward \ --output rtsp://localhost:8554/camera \ --encoder auto --fps 30 --bitrate 4M --duration 60s capturefab --session bench forward --output rtsp://localhost:8554/camera capturefab --session bench stop-forward capturefab doctor --json capturefab ffmpeg --json Frames use a limited queue that keeps the latest frame. A real encoder trial determines availability with the build and host drivers. GPU branding alone does not establish support. --encoder selects the output encoder. The global --hwaccel option controls FFmpeg input decoding. Protocol and codec support depend on the included FFmpeg build. Capturefab does not write local HLS output. A server such as MediaMTX can serve HLS from your published stream. Scanner sources do not support forwarding.

documents.title: Control the app from a script or headless session
documents.summary: Use CLI commands with the camera connection open in the desktop app. Use serve for a persistent session without a window.
documents.body: Record & automate Control the app from a script or headless session Use CLI commands with the camera connection open in the desktop app. Use serve for a persistent session without a window. Camera and session commands automatically attach to the only active authenticated session. With several sessions, specify --session NAME . Without a clear target, commands fail before a change. With no session, supported commands use a temporary worker. --direct --camera ID selects a temporary worker. Use sessions --json to list session names, kinds ( gui or serve ) and active states. The desktop session name defaults to gui . Expand Shell & agents in Capture or use the Quick guide to copy a command for the visible session. capturefab gui --name bench # In another terminal: capturefab sessions --json capturefab connect sim:0 # the only running session capturefab --session bench connect sim:1 capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 set ExposureTime=2500 capturefab --session bench --camera sim:1 capture -o second.png capturefab --session bench status --json # An alternative to the desktop, kept running in the foreground capturefab --camera sim:0 serve --name headless --stream --camera ID targets one camera and keeps the visible selection. select ID sets the session default for CLI calls without --camera . Each desktop window and browser tab keeps its own selection. Use connect ID , disconnect , start and stop to control a persistent camera. CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA supplies a default camera. CAPTUREFAB_SESSION supplies a session for commands that use one. --direct overrides that environment variable. It conflicts only with an explicit --session option. Session environment defaults do not affect GUI startup, server startup or schema output. --camera ID status --json reports camera state with shared activity and cameras . result.target_camera identifies the requested camera. result.active_camera identifies the session default. Desktop windows and browser tabs keep their own camera selection. Use --request-timeout 30s or 5m to limit the full session request. This includes connection, transmission and the response wait. The default depends on the capture count. This deadline is separate from per-frame --timeout-ms and recording --duration . A command can finish in the session after its client times out. Examine status and Activity before retrying a write. Send session JSON directly capturefab schema --json capturefab --session bench rpc --json < command.json # PowerShell: feed the same JSON file to stdin Get-Content command.json -Raw | capturefab --session bench rpc --json Save a command such as {"op":"get","feature":"Width"} in command.json . RPC uses the same operations as workflows. CLI and RPC paths use the calling terminal's directory. This applies to output files, file: , sim:replay: and existing media inputs. Workflow paths use the JSON file's directory. Saved destinations and stream URLs retain their specified meaning. The session server uses loopback TCP and a private local token. Its descriptor and token stay in the private runtime directory. This interface supports local automation. Desktop, CLI and RPC clients share camera state, history and Activity . Binary stdout captures use a temporary worker. They cannot use a persistent session. See the agent instructions and llms.txt for automation guidance. The installed binary’s schema and --help are authoritative for its version.

documents.title: Validate and apply repeatable workflows
documents.summary: Save camera setup, capture, schedule and recording commands in one JSON file. Review the plan before you apply it to a session.
documents.body: Record & automate Validate and apply repeatable workflows Save camera setup, capture, schedule and recording commands in one JSON file. Review the plan before you apply it to a session. Save this example as workflow.json . Each step contains a session command . An outer camera field can select the target camera. The connect and select operations specify the camera inside command . { "version": 1, "steps": [ {"command": {"op": "connect", "camera": "sim:0", "timeout_ms": 2000}}, {"camera": "sim:0", "command": {"op": "set", "feature": "Width", "value": "640"}}, {"camera": "sim:0", "command": { "op": "capture", "output": "shots/first.png", "count": 1, "timeout_ms": 2000, "format": "png" }} ] } capturefab workflow validate workflow.json --json capturefab workflow apply workflow.json --dry-run --json capturefab --session bench workflow apply workflow.json --json # More examples in the source repository capturefab workflow validate examples/workflows/multi-camera-timelapse.json --json Validation and dry runs examine every step without camera access or output files. A document accepts 1–256 steps and a maximum size of 1 MiB. Unknown fields, duplicate fields and invalid values fail before execution. Device capabilities and current storage limits are execution checks. A persistent session is necessary for Apply. It can automatically use the only active session.
